reviews.review:
This game does not respect your time.  I understand it is in early access but there are so many wonky things about it.  I have played many grindy sorts of games ranging from single player RPGs with stupidly rare drops to stuff like MMOs where you kill the same things for hours to level up or find a drop and even with that background I couldn't finish this game.

I will give it credit, it took a concept that tons of people probably wanted from pokemon, just a big open world where you use various pokemon for various purposes, like traversal and battling and cooking food or whatever.  That aspect is cool.  The designs, although some tend to be repetitive with the same model but just with a different element, are overall cool and mostly varied.  The abilities, again, repetitive if they're different elements but some of them look cool.  The world is very big and there's a lot to explore and various ways (grappling, gliding, flying, running, swimming) to do it.

The base building is very bare bones, with a handful of random items and structures you can build to make something that looks base-like.  Base building requires certain stipulations for space otherwise some pals can't move around or do tasks.  They get stuck.  Again, early access, so whatever.

The problem with this game, though, is the pacing.  As you play more and more, the fights get more demanding so you either have to level up or use the right types of pals.  As you get closer to endgame, the fantasy of battling alongside your chosen team of favorite pals goes out the window for nonsense min/maxing that sucks the fun out of the game.  You have to catch or breed HUNDREDS of the same pal to stack it all into one four star superpal to get the best out of their unique partner ability. It's ridiculously grindy, and that doesn't even take into account getting the right passive abilities on your chosen pal(s).  In general, fighting alongside even the strongest pals isn't even the best way to play the game because they have cooldowns.  Instead, players are encouraged by online resources to min/max their own attack stat and do the bulk of the damage themselves while using passive pals that do nothing but sit in your party roster and boost your stats.  While I don't think that shouldn't be an option, there should be multiple ways to succeed at combat including the endgame encounters.

Then there's the weapons, which range from wooden clubs all the way up to pulse rifles and beam swords.  The base weapons you can craft are very mediocre, the really good versions of weapons all being locked behind schematics which are generally found in chests throughout the world completely randomly or in dungeons.  That brings me to my chief complaint, while you can check a map to find where any given dungeon is, the dungeons in-game only spawn at selective times and the game does not tell you when or where they will be.  You could fly around checking 15 dungeon locations and not even find one.  Imagine trying to run a dungeon in an MMO, you have your whole party together, you're ready to play, but you instead spend all your time looking for the dungeon entrance and never find it and just log off for the night. 

 This is really disrespectful of the player's time and ultimately what drove me to quit playing when I hit this point where I wanted to start finding powerful weapons and armor.  Even if you FIND a dungeon, the loot at the end is also random, so you could spend potentially days of playtime looking for one thing you want.

This tedium on top of the sheer amount of repetitive capturing/breeding to stack pals into four star pals as well as the required boring min/maxing ultimately makes me not recommend this game for someone looking for a fun little pokemon-like experience with base building.  I am aware there are server settings to make the combat easier and to increase the amount of pal spawns and drops, but the base game shouldn't require such modifications to be enjoyable.

if they ever address the grinding issues, perhaps make it so schematics are easier to specifically target farm, reduce the number of pals required to make a four star pal, and perhaps have a server setting for dungeons to not be randomized I will revisit it, but as it is now I have no desire to spend hours spinning my wheels for potentially nothing.
